network.tdh.formal.metadataDescription: TDH v1.4 as a Lean 4 model: what it reproduces, what its proofs establish, what turned out to be false, and what the proofs do not cover.
network.tdh.formal.title: Formal model
network.tdh.formal.lede: TDH v1.4 written again in Lean 4, where a computer checks every proof. P26 stays the rule; making the model normative is proposed, not decided. The model’s source is in 6529’s private design repository, so this page reports the manifest its build writes.
network.tdh.formal.summary.provedBody: Of the manifest’s {entries} entries, the theorems Lean’s kernel checked, each using only Lean’s three standard axioms; {byDefinition} of them restate how the model computes a value. With the {cexTheorems} theorems that establish counterexamples they are the {audited} theorems PROOFS.md documents, each with its axioms in the manifest: {proved} + {cexTheorems} = {audited}, {tdh} about TDH v1.4 and {p53} about two validator rules.
network.tdh.formal.summary.falseBody: {kernel} counterexamples are established by a theorem Lean’s kernel checked, and {evaluated} by running the model at every build (#guard, which trusts Lean’s compiler). Counterexamples are not claims: the {firstRule} cases of the first netting rule refute one claim, and each other counterexample refutes a claim of its own, so {claims} claims are shown false. Each is now reflected in P26 or P53.
network.tdh.formal.why.title: Why write the rule again
network.tdh.formal.why.body: Plain English can be read more than one way. A second implementation, written in a clean room from P26, its vectors and the documents P26 cites, recorded 23 places where it had to choose, two of them rated high. P26 now states a rule for each.
network.tdh.formal.why.body2: A formal model removes that ambiguity: every term has one meaning, and the computer rejects a proof with a gap. Whether that meaning is P26’s is checked by people (below). After program B found the flaw in the first netting rule, the model proved, in five cases, that under it steps inside a transaction could change holdings.
network.tdh.formal.featured.title: What the netting theorem proves, and where it stops
network.tdh.formal.featured.plain: Take any two sequences of transfers whose transactions correspond one to one, in the same order: each pair shares one timestamp and one transaction hash, and moves the same net amount of every token for every address. If both replays have a result, under one registry and the same consolidations, they leave every holding stack the same. P26 applies this to the transfers in canonical order.
network.tdh.formal.featured.means: So, within those limits, the order of a transaction’s steps, its round trips and its detours cannot change any holding stack.
network.tdh.formal.featured.limit: It stops there. Three things read the logged steps: the mint facts, the underflow test and the position checks. So a mint and its burn inside one transaction leave every stack unchanged but can make a token eligible, giving a wallet a balance it did not have, and change editions, rates and other holders’ TDH (counterexamples H and I below). A token’s balance and raw days stay the same while its eligibility does, by P26 §7.2’s definitions; that is not a theorem here.
network.tdh.formal.featured.definitions: Its hypotheses, as defined in the model
network.tdh.formal.figure.title: Two inputs, one net movement
network.tdh.formal.figure.desc: Left: one transaction as logged, with three steps: A sends a copy to X, X sends it back, A sends a copy to B. Right: one transaction with one step, A sends a copy to B. Both move the same net amount for every address: A minus one, B plus one, X zero. Replayed with netting, both leave every holding stack the same.
network.tdh.formal.figure.resultNote: A keeps its other copies with their ages; B’s new copy starts at this transaction. Nothing is minted or burned, so no token’s eligibility changes, and balances and raw days are the same too, by P26 §7.2’s definitions (not a theorem).
network.tdh.formal.contains.title: What the model contains
network.tdh.formal.contains.body: One module per part of P26, from canonical decoded inputs to the day’s records and totals. Each definition cites its P26 section, and all arithmetic is on unbounded integers, with the two binary64 roundings emulated exactly.
network.tdh.formal.contains.bodyRaw: One module per part of P26, from the raw Ethereum logs a node reads to the day’s records and totals: which logs count, their positions, decoding and the type of every input value included. Each definition cites its P26 section, and all arithmetic is on unbounded integers, with the two binary64 roundings emulated exactly.
network.tdh.formal.contains.outside: Outside the model: a node’s own reads of Ethereum, state reads and finality, the binding of the result header, and the legacy emulation.
network.tdh.formal.contains.outsideRaw: Outside the model: a node’s own reads (which chain is canonical and finalized, that its log set is complete, the headers it reads, each Meme’s mint limit at the snapshot block), the vector runner’s JSON reader and the legacy emulation. The raw-log rules are definitions, checked by the runs above, not by a theorem.
network.tdh.formal.module.basic: Rounding, addresses, ZERO and DEAD; binary64 by exact integer emulation
network.tdh.formal.module.registry: The parameter registry, its constraints and its Keccak-256 hash
network.tdh.formal.module.inputs: Decoded transfers and delegation events, canonical order and log positions (decoding itself is not modelled at this build)
network.tdh.formal.module.inputsTyped: Decoded transfers and delegation events, the positions of ignored logs, their types, canonical order and log positions
network.tdh.formal.module.logs: Raw logs: their types, which logs count, positions, header order, decoding and the malformed-log rules, a log given raw or decoded
network.tdh.formal.module.cutoff: Cycle day, boundary, snapshot block and header order, whole days
network.tdh.formal.module.eligibility: Eligibility, editions and floors, rates, seasons
network.tdh.formal.module.consolidation: Kept events, pair state, clusters, identity keys
network.tdh.formal.module.holdings: Acquisition stacks, the underflow test, transaction netting, the replay, per-token values
network.tdh.formal.module.arithmetic: RATE, BASE, ADD, the boost in cents, FINAL
network.tdh.formal.module.scores: Boost, records, finals, daily rates, range checks
network.tdh.formal.module.cycle: The whole cycle: records, totals, range checks, output
network.tdh.formal.statements.title: What is proved, and what is not
network.tdh.formal.statements.intro: Every status comes from the proof manifest the build writes: a theorem counts as proved only when Lean’s kernel checked it with no axiom beyond Lean’s three standard ones. Open a row for its theorems and axioms.
network.tdh.formal.statements.caption: Statements, {shown} of {total} shown
network.tdh.formal.entry.deferred: Named in PROOFS.md as not proved
network.tdh.formal.entry.evaluation: Checked by running the model at every build: {checks} checks

network.tdh.formal.st.netting.title: Netting invariance
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.plain: For any two sequences of transfers whose transactions correspond one to one and in order, each pair with one timestamp, one transaction hash and the same net movement of every token per address, every holding stack is the same, when both replays have a result, under one registry and one set of consolidations. So reordering a transaction’s transfers, or inserting a round trip anywhere in it, through a sink or not, changes no stack whenever both versions have a result: each transaction keeps one timestamp and one transaction hash, every net movement stays below 2⁶⁴, and the underflow test passes.
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.scope: Assumes that both replays have a result, that the two inputs’ transactions correspond one to one and in order, each pair sharing one timestamp and one transaction hash (P26 §3.2 requires it and the model checks it), one registry and the same consolidations. Adding or removing a whole transaction, even one that moves nothing, is not covered, and no theorem goes from a day’s input through the canonical sort, which P26 applies first, to the replay. It is about the stacks only: mint facts read the logged steps, so eligibility, and with it a record’s balance and raw days, base, boost and final, can change (the next two rows).
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.title: The replay succeeds on valid input
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.plain: Once the underflow test passes, and, with netting, P26’s transaction rules hold (one timestamp and one transaction hash per transaction, §3.2, and every net movement below 2⁶⁴, §7.1), the replay succeeds, with or without netting, and every stack outside the sinks holds exactly its address’s balance: what it received minus what it sent. That is why P26 need not test for underflow again in the replay.
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.scope: On an input that breaks those rules the theorem says nothing; P26 makes such an input invalid. A sink’s stack is not a balance: sinks are credited but never debited.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.title: Copies are conserved
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.plain: Summed over every address outside the sinks, the copies held of a token are the copies that came from a sink minus those that went to one. An address that never appears holds none.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.scope: The inflow counts transfers from the zero address (mints) and from 0x…dead, which creates copies (P26 §3.4). Holds for any registry’s sinks.
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.title: Identity sums
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.plain: In every day’s result, each identity’s balance, raw days and base TDH, in total and for every token, are the sums over exactly its wallet records, each counted once; and every wallet record belongs to exactly one identity.
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.scope: Not for boost and final, which are computed per record: see “Total = sum of wallets” below.
network.tdh.formal.st.order.title: Order independence
network.tdh.formal.st.order.plain: Reordering the decoded transfers, delegation events and ignored-log positions in any way gives the same result, or the same error, including the log-position checks of P26 §3.1. The order of the decoded items cannot matter.
network.tdh.formal.st.order.scope: A transfer’s position fields are part of the input: changing them changes the canonical order, as it should. Raw logs reach these lists through the decoder, which is outside the model, so the order of raw logs is not covered.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderRaw.title: Order independence, raw logs included
network.tdh.formal.st.orderRaw.plain: With the header timestamps and the claims’ mint limits taken as fixed, reordering the raw logs, the decoded transfers and delegation events and the ignored-log positions, in any way, gives the same result, or no result for both, including the position checks of P26 §3.1 and the type checks of §3.2. The order of the raw logs and of the decoded items cannot change the result.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderRaw.scope: The header timestamps and the claims’ mint limits are inputs held fixed, not reordered. When several raw logs are malformed, which one the error names can depend on their order, so the theorem compares results, not error messages. A transfer’s position fields are part of the input: changing them changes the canonical order, as it should.
network.tdh.formal.st.rawLogs.title: The model from raw logs
network.tdh.formal.st.rawLogs.plain: The model on decoded inputs is the model on raw logs when no log is given raw, so every theorem above about decoded inputs holds there. And a day with a result has every input value at its type: the registry, the snapshot block and time, every transfer, delegation event and log position, every raw log and every header timestamp.
network.tdh.formal.st.rawLogs.scope: The rules for raw logs (which logs count, decoding, positions, header order and types) are definitions, not theorems: P26’s vectors, the October 11 cycle and random inputs check that they say what P26 says. The vector runner’s JSON reader is test tooling and is not proved.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.title: Last in, first out
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.plain: The model’s compact stack is exactly P26’s ordered list: a purchase appends, a send removes exactly the last n entries in order and fails exactly when there are fewer, and its size is its length.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.scope: About how the model stores a stack: it behaves as P26’s list. Which entries the replay pushes and takes is covered by the rows above.
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.title: Totals
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.plain: In every day with a result: the network total is the sum of identity finals, the total without sinks leaves out exactly the sink identities, the base and raw totals are sums too, and the total is below 2⁵³.
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.scope: This restates how the totals are defined; only the range check adds anything. A sum over wallets is a different number: see “Total = sum of wallets”.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.title: P26’s stated numbers
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.plain: The registry hash, the half-cent rate ties for H = 3,941, BASE’s rounding, ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 from 33 sets, no ties in the boost’s rounding, the final ties that round down, removal from the end of a stack, and the positions of ignored logs.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.scope: Evaluated at every build, which trusts Lean’s compiler; not proved in the kernel.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.count: {checks} checks in Tdh/Facts.lean, evaluated at every build.
network.tdh.formal.st.factsTyped.title: P26’s stated numbers
network.tdh.formal.st.factsTyped.plain: The registry hash, the half-cent rate ties for H = 3,941, BASE’s rounding, ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 from 33 sets, no ties in the boost’s rounding, the final ties that round down, removal from the end of a stack, and the positions of ignored logs. Since round 4 also the rule identifier, the types of values (the registry’s, and the full range of 256-bit and signed 64-bit values), which dates are cycle dates, the highest block a cutoff can have, and that a log is given raw or decoded, never both.
network.tdh.formal.st.factsTyped.scope: Evaluated at every build, which trusts Lean’s compiler; not proved in the kernel.
network.tdh.formal.st.beyondStacks.title: Steps inside a transaction never matter
network.tdh.formal.st.beyondStacks.plain: False beyond the stacks. Inserting a mint of 10 copies and its burn into one transaction leaves every stack unchanged, but 10 more copies count as minted: the largest edition doubles, another card’s rate doubles from 2.00 to 4.00, and another holder’s final doubles from 800 to 1,600. A mint and its burn can also make a token eligible: a wallet with no record gets a balance of 5, and another holder goes from 32 to 60.
network.tdh.formal.st.beyondStacks.scope: Counterexamples H and I, checked at every build. Since October 15, P26 §7.1 states the property for the stacks only. Whether such mints should count toward editions is flagged for the owner, not decided.
network.tdh.formal.st.balanceRaw.title: Balances and raw days, when eligibility is unchanged
network.tdh.formal.st.balanceRaw.plain: For every token whose eligibility the steps leave as it was, a record’s balance and raw days stay the same too: both are read from the token’s stacks and the cutoff time.
network.tdh.formal.st.balanceRaw.scope: This follows from P26 §7.2’s definitions, and P26 says so; the model does not prove it as a theorem.
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.title: Held = minted − burned
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.plain: False. A transfer from 0x…dead credits its recipient with a fresh copy and is not a mint. Case G: one copy minted, one sent by 0x…dead, two held. What holds instead is the conservation law above.
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.scope: False by evaluation: counterexample G is a #guard the build evaluates, which trusts Lean’s compiler, not a theorem Lean’s kernel checked. What holds instead, the conservation law above, is proved.
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.title: Total = sum of wallets
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.plain: False. Each record’s boost is computed on its own holdings. Case F is a day with no eligible Meme, so a Gradient’s rate is its 1.00 minimum: two wallets of one identity each hold one Gradient for 100 days, base 100 each. Each wallet record has boost 1.02 and final 102, and the identity has boost 1.04 and final 208. The total is 208, not 204.
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.scope: P26 §7.3 now says so, with this example. A page that adds up wallet values will not match the total.
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.title: The first netting rule
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.plain: False: under D131’s first rule, steps inside a transaction could change even the holding stacks. Five cases are proved in the kernel; the uniform rule P26 adopted the same day gives equal results in each.
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.scope: Values from the model, the first rule’s from its build at 9cd101a: the network total in cases A, D and E, and in case B under the current rule; ZERO’s record in case B under the first rule; and identity {A, B}’s final in case C, after a later sale.
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.title: The 19.99% cap
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.plain: With at least six parties of positive weight, no party, capped or not, counts more than 19.99% of the counted total, and the key slices add up exactly. For the live roster it holds for the registered weight W, because an account is live only while it keeps a valid key; each account’s keys after the no-pool rule and the lease are inputs of the model, not proved. The loop stops within six passes.
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.scope: A separate small model of the cap. Each account’s keys after the no-pool rule, the lease and group membership are inputs, not proved; with fewer than six parties of positive weight there is no cap and the theorems say nothing.
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.title: Exclusions
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.plain: For a node that keeps incident records, each with its step and length fixed when it opens, as P53 §13.1 now prescribes: no evidence shortens an exclusion in force, exclusions never overlap, stretch or repeat, and pruning old records on P53’s schedule changes no exclusion.
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.scope: For a node that recomputes incidents from the evidence it still holds, the claim is false: an exclusion can end 298 cycles early. P53 now rules recomputation out.

network.tdh.formal.not.title: What the proofs do not guarantee
network.tdh.formal.not.english.title: That the English text says the same thing.
network.tdh.formal.not.english.body: People check that the model matches the specification; a disagreement is fixed in one or the other and recorded. P26 settled the questions the model raised on October 15, and in later rounds the findings of the differential tests; its fifth round, on October 16, ruled on every input type the implementations had split on, and the model’s round 5 follows it. On October 18, D136 brought 6529.io’s four-wallet consolidation into P26, and the model’s round 6, committed the same day, follows that. By the model’s PROOFS.md, every question raised is settled but one, flagged for the owner: whether mints inside a transaction should count toward editions (counterexamples H and I).
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.title: That the programs match the model on every input.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.body: The model passes all {vectors} vectors of the P26 its build follows, as both references do, and the model matched the Python reference on one real day, the October 11, 2026 cycle, and on random inputs; in CI, 1,000 seeded random inputs run through Lean, Python and the Rust reference on every change. Six rounds of differential tests ran generated cycles through the model, the Python reference, the Rust core and program B, the sixth on TDH v1.4. As of October 18, 2026 all four programs follow P26 at 3bfa7b0 (D136): the model in its round 6, committed, and the Rust core and program B in the validator’s build a1463f9. Tests can miss cases: no machine-checked proof links any program’s code to the model.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.title: That the inputs are right.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.body: A node’s own reads of Ethereum, state reads and finality are outside the model. Since round 4 (f854661) the rules that select and decode logs are definitions of the model: vectors and runs check that they say what P26 says, no theorem does. Round 5 adds the one-log rule, and proves that the model’s check of it is enough: in the canonical transfers, any two at one log position share its contract, sender and recipient (canonicalTransfers_oneLog). It also makes the vector runner’s JSON reader strict; the reader is test tooling outside the model, checked by vectors only. Checked reads (D118) are built: every daily run checks the snapshot block’s headers against a finalized block and the edition floors against its state, while the history before it is taken as reported until the full check runs. Two separately written programs are being built to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s history (D119).
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.bodyRaw: A node’s own reads are outside the model: which chain is canonical and finalized, that its log set is complete, the headers it reads to find the snapshot block, and each Meme’s mint limit at that block. Since round 4 (f854661) the rules that select and decode logs are definitions of the model: vectors and runs check that they say what P26 says, no theorem does. Round 5 adds the one-log rule, and proves that the model’s check of it is enough: in the canonical transfers, any two at one log position share its contract, sender and recipient (canonicalTransfers_oneLog). It also makes the vector runner’s JSON reader strict; the reader is test tooling outside the model, checked by vectors only. Checked reads (D118) are built: every daily run checks the snapshot block’s headers against a finalized block and the edition floors against its state, while the history before it is taken as reported until the full check runs. Two separately written programs are being built to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s history (D119).
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.title: That the rule is the right rule.
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.body: A proof shows the rule does what it says, not that it is fair or wise. Rule changes are owner decisions.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.title: Lean itself.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.body: The proofs rely on Lean’s small kernel and its three standard axioms. The build audits them for every theorem and definition of the model, and the manifest lists the axioms of each theorem PROOFS.md documents. The checks of P26’s stated facts, the real day and some counterexamples are evaluations, which also trust Lean’s compiler.
network.tdh.formal.layers.title: Three layers of assurance
network.tdh.formal.layers.desc: The English specification is checked against the Lean model by people. Inside the Lean model, the proofs are the only machine-checked links. The model and the programs share one set of conformance vectors; the model was compared with the Python reference on one real day, the October 11, 2026 cycle, and on random inputs, CI runs 1,000 seeded random inputs through Lean, Python and the Rust reference, and four programs were run on generated cycles in six rounds of differential tests. The Rust core and the Python reference check each other in the daily comparison. As decided (D125), every validator is to check the Rust core against program B before it signs; program B is not in the validator yet, and nothing signs today. Checked reads (D118) are built; the history before the snapshot is taken as reported until the full check runs. Proofs A and B (D119) are being built.
network.tdh.formal.layers.programsSub: Rust core, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.formal.layers.vectors: Shared conformance vectors; one real day (October 11, 2026) and random inputs against the Python reference; 1,000 seeded inputs through Lean, Python and Rust in CI; six rounds of generated cycles across four programs
network.tdh.formal.layers.inputsBody: Checked reads (D118), built: every daily run checks the snapshot block’s headers and the edition floors; the history before the snapshot is taken as reported until the full check runs. Proofs A and B (D119): being built.

network.tdh.formal.check.title: How the model is checked
network.tdh.formal.check.body: The model is in 6529’s private design repository, beside the specification and its vectors, so these commands need its source. With it and Lean installed, anyone can rebuild the model, which re-checks every proof and audits its axioms, and run the vectors through it:
network.tdh.formal.check.commands:
lake build                                     # every proof, and the axiom audit
lake exe tdh-vectors ../tdh-reference/vectors  # P26’s conformance vectors
lake exe tdh-vectors vectors-netting           # the netting files
python3 tools/manifest.py                      # the manifest this page reads
network.tdh.formal.summary.vectorsBehind: ; P26 has {latest} since {latestCommit}, after this build
network.tdh.formal.newer.body: Round {round}, at commit {commit}, follows P26 at 3bfa7b0: TDH v1.4, with D136’s four-wallet consolidation. Each direction of a link keeps its registration time, links confirmed in one block are taken by pair key, and a fourth wallet joins only through the gate. It proves that every group holds at most the registry’s maximum of wallets, all pairwise confirmed; that a group past the ungated size has a member whose links with all the others were registered both ways at or after the activation time; and that on a day before that time no group has more than three wallets. It passes all 104 vectors.
network.tdh.formal.featured.scope: Two limits. Adding or removing a whole transaction, even one whose every net movement is zero, is not covered. And no theorem yet goes from a day’s input through P26’s canonical sort to the replay: the theorem compares two sequences as they are given.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderOneLog.title: Order independence, raw logs included
network.tdh.formal.st.orderOneLog.plain: With the header timestamps and the claims’ mint limits taken as fixed, reordering the raw logs, the decoded transfers and delegation events and the ignored-log positions, in any way, gives the same result, or no result for both, including the position checks and the one-log rule of P26 §3.1 and the type checks of §3.2. Also proved: in the canonical transfers, any two at one log position share its contract, sender and recipient.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderOneLog.scope: The header timestamps and the claims’ mint limits are taken as fixed. When several raw logs are malformed, which one the error names can depend on their order, so the theorem compares results, not error messages. A transfer’s position fields are part of the input: changing them changes the canonical order, as it should.

network.tdh.formal.found.title: Found by the model, by program B and by a review, and settled in the specifications
network.tdh.formal.found.firstRule.title: The first netting rule (October 15).
network.tdh.formal.found.firstRule.body: After program B found the flaw, the model proved in the kernel, in five cases, that steps inside a transaction could change holdings under it; P26 made netting uniform.
network.tdh.formal.found.eligibility.tit: Values beyond the stacks (cases H and I).
network.tdh.formal.found.eligibility.bod: A mint and its burn inside one transaction leave every stack unchanged but can change eligibility, rates and other holders’ finals: the model found case H, and a review case I. P26 §7.1 now states its property for the stacks only.
network.tdh.formal.found.sums.title: Identity sums (case F).
network.tdh.formal.found.sums.body: An identity’s final is not the sum of its wallets’ finals; P26 §7.3 now says so, and that balance, raw and base do sum is a theorem.
network.tdh.formal.found.sinks.title: Conservation (case G).
network.tdh.formal.found.sinks.body: Copies held are not minted minus burned when a sink sends: a send from 0x…dead credits a fresh copy and is not a mint (P26 §3.4). What holds, and is proved, counts every sink’s sends.
network.tdh.formal.found.incidents.title: Exclusions (validator rules).
network.tdh.formal.found.incidents.body: A node that recomputed its incidents from pruned evidence could end an exclusion 298 cycles early; P53 §13.1 now fixes each incident’s length when it opens.
network.tdh.formal.found.cap.title: The 19.99% cap (validator rules).
network.tdh.formal.found.cap.body: P53 said the cap’s loop takes at most five passes; the model showed that six can be needed, a loop stopped at five ending on a stale level, and that a party whose accounts keep no valid key could count more than 19.99%. P53 §6.2 and §6.3 now say six passes, make holding a valid key part of being live, and state the cap level as one floor, citing the proof.

network.tdh.formal.st.factsRound5.title: P26’s stated numbers
network.tdh.formal.st.factsRound5.plain: The registry hash, the half-cent rate ties for H = 3,941, BASE’s rounding, ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 from 33 sets, no ties in the boost’s rounding, the final ties that round down, removal from the end of a stack, and the positions of ignored logs. Since round 4 also the rule identifier, the types of values (the registry’s, and the full range of 256-bit and signed 64-bit values), which dates are cycle dates, the highest block a cutoff can have, and that a log is given raw or decoded, never both. Since round 5 also an amount’s type (a uint256, and below 2⁶⁴ at or before the snapshot block), the types of totalMax and its Meme id, and that transfers at one log position must share its contract, sender and recipient.
network.tdh.formal.st.factsRound5.scope: Evaluated at every build, which trusts Lean’s compiler; not proved in the kernel.

network.tdh.formal.st.clusters.title: Group sizes and the four-wallet gate
network.tdh.formal.st.clusters.claim: Every identity stays within the registry’s limits, and a fourth wallet joins only through the gate.
network.tdh.formal.st.clusters.plain: In every result of a day, each identity’s wallets are distinct, at most the registry’s maximum of them (four under tdh-v1.4), and any two of them have a confirmed link; an identity larger than the registry’s ungated size (three) has a member whose links with all the others were registered in both directions at or after the activation time. On a day whose snapshot is before that time, no identity has more than three wallets.
network.tdh.formal.st.clusters.scope: The theorems say which wallets may share an identity, not which of several possible groups the greedy order picks: that order, newest block first, then ascending pair key, is pinned by vectors 89 to 99 and was checked against 6529.io’s own code on 100,000 random link graphs. That the pair-key order is the order of the sorted addresses is checked by #guard on examples, and that P26 §6.2 and §6.3 are 6529.io’s code is a statement about the text, which vectors and the references test; neither is a theorem.

network.tdh.formal.st.netting.claim: For transfers already in canonical order whose transactions correspond one to one, steps inside a transaction cannot change any holding stack, when both have a result.
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.claim: On valid input the replay succeeds, and each stack outside the sinks holds its address’s balance.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.claim: Copies held outside the sinks are those that came from a sink minus those sent to one.
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.claim: An identity’s balance, raw days and base are the sums of its wallets’.
network.tdh.formal.st.order.claim: The order of the decoded inputs cannot change the result.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderRaw.claim: With the headers and claim limits fixed, the order of the raw logs cannot change the result.
network.tdh.formal.st.orderOneLog.claim: With the headers and claim limits fixed, the order of the raw logs cannot change the result; transfers at one log position agree.
network.tdh.formal.st.rawLogs.claim: The model from raw logs agrees with the model on decoded inputs.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.claim: The model’s stack behaves exactly as P26’s list: last in, first out.
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.claim: The totals are the sums P26 defines, and stay below 2⁵³.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.claim: The numbers P26 states hold at every build.
network.tdh.formal.st.factsTyped.claim: The numbers P26 states hold at every build.
network.tdh.formal.st.factsRound5.claim: The numbers P26 states hold at every build.
network.tdh.formal.st.beyondStacks.claim: False beyond the stacks: a mint and its burn can change other values.
network.tdh.formal.st.balanceRaw.claim: Balances and raw days follow the stacks while eligibility is unchanged.
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.claim: False: a send from 0x…dead creates a copy that is not a mint.
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.claim: False: an identity’s final is not the sum of its wallets’ finals.
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.claim: False: under the first netting rule, steps inside a transaction changed stacks.
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.claim: With six or more parties of positive weight, none counts more than 19.99%; six passes suffice.
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.claim: For a node that keeps its incident records, no exclusion in force is shortened, and none overlaps or repeats.
network.tdh.formal.legend.shownFalseEval: a counterexample evaluated at every build
network.tdh.formal.not.english.short: People check that the model matches the specification. Every question raised is settled but one, flagged for the owner: whether mints inside a transaction count toward editions.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.short: The programs pass the same vectors and agree on generated inputs; the Rust core is checked against the Python reference on each day of the daily comparison, and the Lean model matched it on one real day, October 11, 2026. No machine-checked proof links any program’s code to the model.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.short: A node’s own reads of Ethereum are outside the model. Checked reads are built; the history before the snapshot is taken as reported until the full check runs.
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.short: A proof shows the rule does what it says, not that it is fair or wise. Rule changes are owner decisions.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.short: The proofs trust Lean’s small kernel and its three standard axioms; the evaluated checks also trust its compiler.
